mainTopic: רבי שמעון's ladder of atonement for the goats of ראש חודש, the רגלים, and יום הכפורים, followed by רבי יוחנן's ruling that unneeded תמיד lambs may be redeemed while unblemished.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that the outer goat of יום הכפורים is compared by a היקש to the inner goat. Then the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון בן יהודה's version of רבי שמעון's view in the משנה. In this version the goats of ראש חודש, the רגלים, and יום הכפורים form a ladder, and each covers more kinds of sin than the one below. Twice the גמרא asks why the lower goat cannot cover what the higher one covers, and each time it answers from a word in a פסוק. Each time it then challenges that the higher goat should not cover the lower one's sins either. In the second round the answer that רבי שמעון ignores 'אחת' is examined. In the end the גמרא concludes that he does learn from 'אחת', and only 'על קרנותיו' limits the inner goat to one atonement. A new topic follows: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן that unneeded תמיד lambs may be redeemed while unblemished. רב חסדא objects that their holiness cannot just disappear. רבה answers with a proof from leftover קטורת. רב חסדא replies that קטורת is different, and his reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the source: the outer goat is compared to the inner goat
steps.stepSummary: The end of a פסוק about the יום הכפורים offerings links the outer goat to the inner goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...the sin-offering of the atonements.' So the outer goat is compared to the inner goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from the previous lines. It quotes the end of a פסוק and concludes that the outer goat of יום הכפורים is compared to the inner goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the outer goat ('one goat for a sin-offering') right next to the inner goat ('the sin-offering of the atonements'). Because they are mentioned together, the גמרא makes a היקש between them. Whatever limits apply to what the inner goat atones for also apply to the outer goat.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin-offering of atonements; here it means the inner goat of יום הכפורים
Was compared (by a היקש), so that the two share the same rules
The outer one: the goat whose service is done outside, in the courtyard
The inner one: the goat whose blood is brought inside, into the קודש הקדשים

steps.whatToRemember: Through a היקש from במדבר 29:11, the outer goat of יום הכפורים shares the limits of the inner goat.

phrases.english: 'the sin-offering of the atonements'
phrases.notes: This is the end of a פסוק that started before this point: במדבר 29:11.

phrases.english: and so the outer goat is compared to the inner goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The outer goat is linked by היקש to the inner goat and shares its limits.

steps.title: Quoting the second version of רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי שמעון בן יהודה reports a different version of רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in his name, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה so that it can discuss it next. This line sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the goats are arranged like a ladder. The ראש חודש goats atone for a טהור person who ate טמא קדשים. The רגלים goats atone for that, and also for cases where the person was never aware of the sin, neither at the start nor at the end. The יום הכפורים goat atones for both of those, and also for cases where the person became aware only at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: In his name, here meaning in the name of רבי שמעון
Etc.; the rest of the משנה is not quoted

steps.confusionAlert: This is a second version of רבי שמעון's view. In this version, each higher goat covers everything the lower goat covers, plus more. Do not mix it up with the first version in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says
in his name, etc.
phrases.notes: 'His name' means רבי שמעון. The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, which lists what each goat atones for.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the second version of רבי שמעון's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראש חודש goats atone for one case, רגלים goats for two, and the יום הכפורים goat for three, with each including the ones below it.

steps.title: Why can't the ראש חודש goats cover what the רגלים goats cover?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ראש חודש goats are limited and do not atone for the extra sin that the רגלים goats atone for.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the ראש חודש goats, that they do not atone for what the רגלים goats atone for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the ladder. Why do the ראש חודש goats stop at one kind of sin, when the רגלים goats cover more?
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these are goats brought as a חטאת for the community. So why should one kind cover less than another? The גמרא is looking for a source in the פסוק that limits the ראש חודש goats.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason two cases are treated differently
New Moons; the goats brought on ראש חודש
The Festivals; the goats brought on the holidays
They atone

phrases.english: What is different about the goats of the New Moons
that they do not atone for what the Festival goats atone for?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים דְּלָא מְכַפְּרִי אַדִּרְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first rung of the ladder in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that limits the ראש חודש goats to one kind of sin.

steps.title: The word עון teaches: one sin only
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'עון' (sin) in the singular, so the ראש חודש goat atones for only one sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says 'the sin': it bears one sin and does not bear two sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק. The word 'עון' is singular, so the ראש חודש goat atones for only one kind of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא 10:17 talks about a ראש חודש goat. It says it was given 'to bear the sin of the congregation.' Since 'sin' is singular, this goat is limited to one sin, and so it cannot also cover what the רגלים goats cover.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin (singular)
Bears, carries; here it means atones for
As the פסוק says; introduces a source

phrases.english: As the verse says: 'sin'
it bears one sin
and does not bear two sins.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular 'עון' limits the ראש חודש goat to atoning for one sin.

steps.title: Then the רגלים goats shouldn't cover the ראש חודש sin either
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אותה' in the same פסוק seems to say that only the ראש חודש goat bears its sin, so the רגלים goats should not cover it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the רגלים goats should also not atone for what the ראש חודש goats atone for! The פסוק says 'it': it bears the sin, and nothing else bears that sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ladder from the other direction. The same פסוק says 'אותה' (it), which seems to say that only this goat can atone for this sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we read words in this פסוק so closely, then 'אותה' should teach that the ראש חודש sin is covered only by the ראש חודש goat. If that were true, the רגלים goats could not include the ראש חודש sin, which goes against the ladder in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It (her); a word that can be read as limiting: 'this one, and no other'
Also
No other

phrases.aramaic: דִּרְגָלִים נָמֵי לָא נִיכַפְּרוּ אַדְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים –
phrases.english: Then the Festival goats should also not atone for what the New Moon goats atone for,
as the verse says: 'it'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק: 'and He gave it to you to bear the sin of the congregation.'

phrases.english: it bears the sin
and nothing else bears the sin!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּרְגָלִים נָמֵי לָא נִיכַפְּרוּ אַדְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same close reading as step 4 to attack the משנה's ladder.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 2 that the רגלים goats also cover the ראש חודש sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אותה' should limit the ראש חודש sin to the ראש חודש goat alone.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not learn from אותה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not draw any lesson from the word 'אותה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not learn anything from 'it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון does not read 'אותה' as a limit. So nothing stops the רגלים goats from covering the ראש חודש sin too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learns from 'עון' (one sin only) but not from 'אותה'. So the ראש חודש goat is limited to one sin, but the sin itself is not limited to that goat.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not mean anything to him; he does not learn from it

phrases.english: He does not learn anything from 'it.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the reading: the word is not treated as a limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותה' limits the ראש חודש sin to the ראש חודש goat alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון does not learn from 'אותה', so the רגלים goats can cover two sins.

steps.title: Why can't the רגלים goats cover what the יום הכפורים goat covers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רגלים goats do not atone for the extra case that the יום הכפורים goat covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the רגלים goats, that they do not atone for what the יום הכפורים goat atones for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves up to the next rung of the ladder. It asks why the רגלים goats cannot cover the special case of the יום הכפורים goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question has the same pattern as step 3. Now the גמרא wants the source that keeps the case where the person became aware only at the end for יום הכפורים alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement; here, its outer goat

phrases.english: What is different about the Festival goats
that they do not atone for what the goats of Yom Kippur atone for?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא דִּרְגָלִים דְּלָא מְכַפְּרִי אַדְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 3, now for the next rung of the ladder.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that keeps the special case of יום הכפורים away from the רגלים goats.

steps.title: 'Once a year' keeps that atonement for יום הכפורים only
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'אחת בשנה' teaches that this atonement happens only once a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says 'once a year': this atonement should happen only once a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the פסוק 'once a year.' The special atonement of יום הכפורים can happen only on that one day, so no other goat can do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אחת בשנה' sets the יום הכפורים atonement apart. The case it covers can be atoned for only on יום הכפורים, never by the רגלים goats.

keyTerms.meaning: Once a year
Atonement

phrases.english: As the verse says: 'once a year'
this atonement should be only
once a year.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אחת בשנה' limits that special atonement to יום הכפורים alone.

steps.title: Then יום הכפורים shouldn't cover the רגלים sins either
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אחת' could mean the goat does only one atonement, so the יום הכפורים goat should not also cover the רגלים cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the יום הכפורים goat should also not atone for what the רגלים goats atone for! It says 'one': it makes one atonement and not two atonements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again from the other direction. 'אחת' could mean one atonement only, which would stop the יום הכפורים goat from also covering the lower cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we read 'אחת' closely, it could limit the יום הכפורים goat to a single kind of atonement. That would break the ladder, because the משנה says this goat covers three cases.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a challenge based on what was just said
'One' is written
Two atonements

phrases.english: If so, the goats of Yom Kippur also
should not atone for what the Festival goats atone for,
since 'once' is written,
it makes one atonement
and does not make two atonements!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים נָמֵי לָא נִיכַפְּרוּ אַדִּרְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 5, now aimed at the יום הכפורים goat.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 2 that the יום הכפורים goat also covers the רגלים cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אחת' should limit the goat to one atonement only.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not learn from אחת
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not draw a lesson from the single word 'אחת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not learn anything from 'one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון does not read 'אחת' as 'only one atonement.' So the יום הכפורים goat can cover all three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is simply that רבי שמעון does not read 'אחת' as a limit, so the יום הכפורים goat can cover all three cases. This answer raises a problem of its own, because step 8 relied on that same phrase. The next steps ask why he ignores 'אחת', and step 14 ends up revising this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: One / once

steps.whatToRemember: In both rounds the pattern is the same. One word limits the lower goat, and the גמרא answers that רבי שמעון does not learn from the word that would limit the higher goat. For 'אחת', step 14 revises this: he does learn from it, and the limit to one atonement comes from 'על קרנותיו' instead.

phrases.english: He does not learn anything from 'once.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the reading: the word is not treated as a limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אחת' limits the יום הכפורים goat to one atonement.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון does not learn from 'אחת', so the יום הכפורים goat covers three cases.

steps.title: Why doesn't he learn from 'once'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון does not draw a lesson from the word 'אחת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the last step: why doesn't רבי שמעון learn anything from the word 'אחת'? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 we were told that רבי שמעון does not expound 'אחת'. The גמרא wants a reason, because a word in the תורה is normally expected to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?

phrases.english: Why?
phrases.notes: He means: why doesn't רבי שמעון learn anything from the word 'אחת', as we said in the last step?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the answer given in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי שמעון does not learn from the word 'אחת'.

steps.title: 'Once' is written about the inside goat
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אחת' is written about the goat whose blood is brought inside the היכל, so it says nothing about the outside goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because when the word 'once' is written, it is written about the goat that is done inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: 'אחת' appears in a פסוק about the inside goat, so it cannot limit the outside goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two goats on יום הכפורים: one whose blood is brought inside, and one offered outside. Since 'אחת' is said about the inside goat, its limit of 'only one atonement' does not apply to the outside goat. So the outside goat can also atone for the רגלים cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat whose blood service is done inside the היכל on יום הכפורים
It is written

phrases.english: Because when 'once' is written,
it is written about the goat that is done inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי כְּתִיב ״אַחַת״ בְּשָׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בִּפְנִים כְּתִיב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אחת' is said about the inside goat, so it does not limit the outside goat.

steps.title: Then the festival goats should atone like the יום הכפורים goat
steps.stepSummary: If 'אחת' only speaks about the inside goat, then the 'once a year' rule should not stop the רגלים goats from atoning for what the outside יום הכפורים goat atones for.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the goats of the festivals should also atone for what the goat of יום הכפורים atones for, because when 'once' is written, it is written about the goat that is done inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer against itself. If 'אחת' only talks about the inside goat, then the rule from step 8 falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the גמרא used 'אחת בשנה' to show that the רגלים goats cannot atone for the יום הכפורים goat's case, because that atonement happens only once a year. But now we said 'אחת' is about the inside goat only. If so, it should say nothing about the outside goat, and the רגלים goats should be able to share its atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
They should atone

phrases.english: If so,
the goats of the festivals should also atone for what the goat of יום הכפורים atones for,
phrases.notes: This is the outside goat of יום הכפורים, the one offered on the outer altar.

phrases.english: because when 'once' is written,
it is written about the goat that is done inside!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, דִּרְגָלִים נָמֵי נְכַפְּרוּ אַדְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 12 undoes the rule from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that 'אחת' applies only to the inside goat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'אחת' says nothing about the outside goat, then 'אחת בשנה' cannot keep the רגלים goats from atoning for the outside goat's case, which goes against step 8.

steps.title: 'On its corners' limits only the inner altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does learn from 'אחת'. But the limit of 'only one atonement' comes from 'על קרנותיו', which speaks about the inner altar, so the outside goat can bring two atonements.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he does learn from 'once'. But here it is different, because the פסוק says: 'And אהרן shall atone on its corners once a year.' It is the corners of the inner altar that bring one atonement and not two atonements. But the outer altar can bring even two atonements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back its earlier answer and gives a better one. 'אחת' does apply to the outside goat as well, so step 8 stands. The limit to just one atonement comes from a different phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two ideas are separated. 'אחת בשנה' teaches that this atonement happens only once a year, so the רגלים goats cannot share it. The words 'על קרנותיו' (the corners of the inner altar) teach that only the inside goat is limited to one atonement. The outside goat, brought on the outer altar, can cover two kinds of cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (the גמרא is taking back the earlier answer)
He does learn from it
Here it is different
Its corners, the horn-like corners of the altar
The inner (golden) altar / the outer altar

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון: 'אחת בשנה' means the יום הכפורים atonement happens only once a year, so the רגלים goats can't do it. 'על קרנותיו' limits only the inside goat to one atonement, so the outside goat can bring two.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two lessons. 'Once a year' is about how often the atonement happens. 'Only one atonement' is about how many kinds of cases one goat covers, and that limit applies only to the inner altar.

phrases.english: Really, he does learn from 'once';
phrases.notes: This takes back step 10. רבי שמעון does learn from 'אחת', and it covers the outside goat too.

phrases.english: but here it is different, because the פסוק says:
'And אהרן shall atone on its corners
once a year' —
it is the corners of the inner altar
that atone with one atonement
and do not atone with two atonements,
but the outer one can bring even two atonements.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם ״אַחַת״ מַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ; וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by replacing the answer of steps 10 and 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes back the earlier claim and finds the limit in a different phrase of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון does not learn from 'אחת' at all, since it is written about the inside goat.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחת' does apply to the outside goat (once a year). Only 'על קרנותיו' limits the inside goat to one atonement, so the outside goat may bring two.

steps.title: Unneeded daily offerings are redeemed while unblemished
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן: lambs set aside for the תמיד that the ציבור did not end up needing may be redeemed even though they have no blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: daily-offering lambs that the community did not need are redeemed even when unblemished.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. עולא reports a ruling of רבי יוחנן about leftover lambs bought for the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an animal set aside as a קרבן cannot be redeemed unless it gets a blemish. רבי יוחנן says that leftover תמיד lambs that were not used are an exception. They may be redeemed while still whole.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily communal offerings
The community / public
They are redeemed (made non-holy by paying their value)
Unblemished, whole

phrases.english: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
daily-offering lambs that were not needed by the community
are redeemed while unblemished.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unneeded תמיד lambs may be redeemed even without a blemish.

steps.title: רב חסדא: where did their holiness go?
steps.stepSummary: While רבה is teaching רבי יוחנן's ruling, רב חסדא challenges it: these lambs had holiness built into them, so how can that holiness disappear?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה was sitting and teaching this ruling. רב חסדא said to him: Who will listen to you and to רבי יוחנן your teacher? The holiness that was in them, where did it go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first sets the scene: רבה is teaching רבי יוחנן's ruling. Then רב חסדא attacks it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These lambs were set aside to be brought on the altar, so their body itself is holy. Holiness like that is not supposed to go away through redemption. So רב חסדא asks how the lambs could become unholy.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching / ruling
Who will listen to you?
Holiness
Where did it go?

phrases.english: רבה was sitting
and teaching this ruling.
רב חסדא said to him:
Who will listen to you
and to רבי יוחנן, your teacher?
The holiness that was in them —
where did it go?
phrases.notes: He means: these lambs were holy in their very body, and that kind of holiness can't just go away by redeeming them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן צָיֵית לָךְ וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the scene with רבה teaching step 15, then challenges that ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that unneeded תמידין are redeemed while unblemished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animals set aside for the altar are holy in their very body, and that holiness cannot be removed by redemption without a blemish.

steps.title: רבה brings a proof from leftover incense
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells רב חסדא that even he must agree we do not ask 'where did the holiness go?', and quotes a משנה about leftover קטורת that was redeemed and bought back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to רב חסדא: Don't you also hold that we do not ask 'The holiness that was in them, where did it go?' We learned in a משנה: What did they do with leftover קטורת? They set aside the craftsmen's wages from the Temple funds. They moved the holiness of the קטורת onto the craftsmen's money. They gave the קטורת to the craftsmen as their pay. Then they bought it back with money from the new year's collection.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends רבי יוחנן by quoting a משנה about leftover קטורת. In that case, holy material that had nothing wrong with it was still redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said holiness cannot just disappear from the lambs. רבה points to a case where it clearly does leave: perfectly good קטורת loses its holiness by being redeemed onto the craftsmen's money. If that works for קטורת, it should also work for the unneeded lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: "The holiness that was in them, where did it go?" This was רב חסדא's challenge.
The incense left over at the end of the year.
Craftsmen who worked for the בית המקדש.
They redeem it, meaning they move its holiness onto money.
The new year's collection of שקלים money.

steps.confusionAlert: The incense was not damaged or bad in any way. That is exactly the point: it was redeemed while it was still perfectly fit, just like the lambs that have no blemish.

phrases.english: He said to him: Don't you also hold
phrases.notes: רבה is speaking to רב חסדא.

But didn't we learn in a משנה:

with money from the new collection.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרַהּ דְּלָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's challenge from step 16 by bringing a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that unneeded תמיד lambs can be redeemed without a blemish, and that 'where did the holiness go?' is not a real problem.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שקלים about leftover קטורת that is redeemed onto the craftsmen's wages and bought back with new funds.

steps.title: רבה spells out the point of the proof
steps.stepSummary: רבה shows that if 'where did the holiness go?' were a real problem, the קטורת method could never work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why does this method work? Let us ask: 'The holiness that was in the incense, where did it go?' Since the משנה allows it, that question must not be a real problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his proof. He asks רב חסדא's own question about the קטורת to show that the משנה clearly does not treat it as a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets fit, holy קטורת be redeemed with no trouble. If רב חסדא's question were valid, it would block the קטורת too. Since it does not, רב חסדא's question cannot block the lambs either.

keyTerms.meaning: "But why?" It asks why something works or is allowed.
"Let us say." It suggests an argument that seems to follow.
"Went" (from the root הלך). In this phrase it is not the word for Jewish law.

phrases.english: But why does this work?
Let us say: 'The holiness that was in it, where did it go?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That 'where did the holiness go?' is not a valid objection.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the משנה about leftover קטורת allows redemption without asking this question.

steps.title: רב חסדא says incense is different
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the proof: you cannot compare קטורת to the תמיד lambs, because קטורת is a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רבה: You bring a proof from קטורת? קטורת is different, (and the reason comes next).
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes away רבה's proof by saying קטורת is a special case. The גמרא is setting up his reason, which continues in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not argue with the משנה. He only says its rule about קטורת does not carry over to animals set aside for the תמיד. So the proof does not reach the lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: "You are saying?" Here it means "You're bringing a proof from that?"
"It is different." This is a standard way to push a proof away.
The incense burned in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: He said to him: You bring a proof from incense?
phrases.notes: Now רב חסדא is answering רבה.

phrases.english: Incense is different,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קְטוֹרֶת קָאָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי קְטוֹרֶת
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison between קטורת and the תמיד lambs. The משנה's ruling itself is not challenged.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: קטורת has a special status that animals for the תמיד do not share. The details continue in the next line.
